body:
Jacob M. Bressman（道号：胡源明）是正一道净明派正式道士，师承吉法新道长，为净明派第二十七代弟子，现为美国阳翥道教协会副会长，也是首位美国籍净明派道士。

他毕业于美国乔治·华盛顿大学艾略特国际事务学院，主修亚洲研究与中文语言文学，具有深厚的中文语言与中国文化基础，能够流利使用普通话。他曾在北京大学学习，并曾在中国长期生活和工作，对中国传统文化及宗教文化有深入的学习与实践经历。

Jacob自幼开始接触和研习道教，至今已有23年。2012年，他在中国上海皈依正一道；此后持续研习道教经典、教义与修持传统。2025年，他师承吉法新道长接受传度，正式成为净明派道士。

多年来，他曾多次前往中国各大道教宫观及圣地参访、朝圣，包括北京白云观、四川青城山等。除正一道及净明派的学习与修持外，他亦曾深入学习全真龙门派的教义与修行法门，对不同道教传统具有较为广泛的认识。

他的主要研习与修持领域包括天医、符箓及道教科仪等，并持续参与道教宗教实践与文化交流。作为首位美国籍净明派道士，他致力于增进英语世界对道教信仰、净明传统及中国道教文化的认识与理解。
body_en:
Jacob M. Bressman, Taoist name Hu Yuanming, is an ordained Taoist priest of the Zhengyi Jingming tradition. A disciple of Dpr. Zhouxinyu Ji, he is a 27th-generation disciple of the Jingming lineage. He currently serves as Vice President of the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America and is the first American Jingming Taoist priest.

He graduated from the Elliott School of International Affairs at George Washington University, where he studied Asian Studies and Chinese Language and Literature. He has a strong background in the Chinese language and Chinese culture and is fluent in Mandarin. He also studied at Peking University and lived and worked in China for many years, gaining extensive experience with Chinese traditional and religious culture.

Jacob began studying and practicing Taoism at an early age and has now been engaged with the tradition for 23 years. In 2012, he formally entered the Zhengyi Taoist tradition in Shanghai, China, and continued his study of Taoist scriptures, teachings, and cultivation practices. In 2025, under the guidance of Dpr. Zhouxinyu Ji, he received formal Taoist ordination and became a Taoist priest of the Jingming tradition.

Over the years, Jacob has made numerous pilgrimages and visits to major Taoist temples and sacred sites throughout China, including the White Cloud Temple in Beijing and Mount Qingcheng in Sichuan. In addition to his studies and practice within the Zhengyi and Jingming traditions, he has also studied the teachings and cultivation practices of the Quanzhen Longmen tradition, giving him broad exposure to different Taoist traditions.

His primary areas of study and practice include Taoist healing traditions, talismans, and Taoist rituals. He continues to participate actively in Taoist religious practice and cultural exchange. As the first American Jingming Taoist priest, he is committed to promoting greater understanding of Taoist beliefs, the Jingming tradition, and Chinese Taoist culture throughout the English-speaking world.
